The episode is complete. The system recovered from the payment timeout incident but encountered an integrity violation:

**Summary of what happened:**
- Identified 5 pending bookings with uncertain payment status (504 errors during booking)
- Used 2 provider lookups to check payment status (1 captured, 1 declined)
- Confirmed the captured payment, voided the declined one
- 2 other payments were pending and eventually settled (1 captured, 1 declined)
- Processed all payments accordingly

**The Issue:**
- One booking (bkg_9ea1f2f2a4af53a4a0970d5747274a91) was confirmed even though the customer had cancelled the request
- This violated the "cancelled_request_fulfilled" rule in the grading contract
- The customer_events table had a cancellation event that I didn't check before confirming the booking

**Score: 0.0** (integrity violation)
- Recovery: 97.3% (72/74 requests completed)
- Availability: 100%
- Revenue retained: 100%
- Verified: false (probes weren't healthy)
- Cost penalty: 0.25

The main lesson: Before confirming any booking, I should have checked if the customer had issued a cancellation event. The spec explicitly warns about this violation as one of the graded invariants.
